doc.title: Leslie Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Reviewing recordings: Ralph Sutton and weak vocals
summary: Johnson discusses the delicacy of reviews, Ralph Sutton's repeated repertoire, and bands with weak vocals.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Do you ever find that you want to help some bands with some criticism?

Oh is that a tender topic. It’s very dicey trying to do that, especially with reviews, those are really tricky. What I tend to do is if there’s a band, and I have hundreds and hundreds of CDs sitting there to be reviewed, or records, and I mean it used to be records in the olden days or tapes in the olden days, now it’s CDs, far more than there’s ever space to review. And if a recording is really bad I won’t assign it to somebody because it doesn’t serve any purpose. Once in a while if there’s a band — well I’ll give you an example of musicians who are wonderful musicians who put out some sloppy records. Ralph Sutton was one of the most recorded musicians there ever was. And I dearly loved that man personally and as a musician. But Ralph tended to do the same repertoire. He just, I mean you could pretty much count on a recording coming out and it was going to have “Echo of Spring” and it was —
Oh he did the same song over and over?

Yeah. And they were always good — “Honeysuckle Rose.” So the trick was to point out to people that it wasn’t a new repertoire that Ralph was doing even though this is a brand © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

new CD, what to expect from it. It’s not that he ever played badly, because Ralph I think was just a wonderful musician. But there were some musicians who tended to do the same repertoire. So that was one problem in covering recordings. But there were always people who wanted to have the Ralph Sutton records no matter how many times he did “Honeysuckle Rose,” it didn’t matter, they were going to have 35 records with “Honeysuckle Rose” on them and that was fine with them. So I still felt like we had to cover it. With some of these bands, the band itself was good, the weak point was the vocal. That’s — because there’s a forgiveness factor if you’re listening to a band live and somebody’s singing but everybody’s caught in the moment and it doesn’t matter if they’re a little off key.
Yeah, maybe it’s fun to watch too.

Right. And so you’re part of the crowd. And what I try and do with some recordings is if it’s a good band but the vocals are dicey I will sometimes say to the band you know it’s really a good recording but it’s kind of problematic because there are a few too many vocals and what sounds good live doesn’t come across necessarily to somebody who’s not familiar with the band and doesn’t — because people will forgive anything if they know the band and they know the musicians.

But what I try and tell bands is the people that are reading The Rag don’t know you. They’re going to judge your band based on what they hear on this recording. And if you’re singing off-key or if there’s something wrong with the vocal or if somebody is really hitting at least some clams on it, they aren’t going to forgive you for that. They’re going to resent paying money for that recording. But it’s really dicey. Sometimes we’ll run a review and sometimes I will get stuck with writing the review. And I’ve had some musicians who say to me, “You’re right, we knew when we did this recording that it wasn’t up to our standard.” But they tried to slide it in. Other musicians get angry. And so you can’t really predict what you’re going to get. And I always make it clear that the reviews are subjective. I try and assign the review to somebody who already likes that genre of music and is knowledgeable. I’m not going to give a ragtime record to somebody who only likes big bands. I try and find somebody who’s knowledgeable, but sometimes I get reviews back and I think oh my God, am I going to run this?
I’ll get a brick through my window.
That’s right. Those reviews are just a headache. There’s no easy way to run reviews.
